gap_reasons: The delivered contribution is the uniform-law zero-gap classification and an endpoint computation and attainment package for a covariate-free, exact-event/known-Uniform-inspection experiment. The canonical operator and efficient direct/indirect estimation already belong to [Bickel–Ritov's framework](https://public.websites.umich.edu/~yritov/IH.pdf), while [Li–Li's Section 6](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10357v2) poses the RMST comparison in a broader mixed-censoring setting. The note keeps this specialization explicit and supplies its inference proof, so there is no stale claim that the broader question or an open attainment step has been settled. Its strict witness establishes positivity without establishing materially useful relative gains, and its fitted-law numerical enclosures exclude sampling uncertainty about the population gain. This narrow theoretical increment, together with the absence of population-gap inference or reproducible finite-sample evidence supporting the proposed precision-assessment use, earns subfield rather than field and constrains the projected paper score to 5.0. tldr: Two compatible sources identify the same randomized causal RMST contrast. In the covariate-free exact-event and known Uniform-inspection experiment, scalar sourcewise efficient means lose information exactly when at least one arm law is nonuniform. The exact gap characterization holds throughout the positive-density surrounding model \(\mathcal M\). On the fixed primitive class \(\mathcal R\), a coercive endpoint boundary problem gives a certified computation, and an explicit histogram, Galerkin and same-function correction procedure attains its original-record variance with uniform studentized .90 coverage. Its fitted systems have order \((n/\log n)^{1/3}\) unknowns. The contribution is this specialized comparison and constructive inference package; generic coarsening efficiency and smooth current-status estimation retain their prior attribution.
gap: Li and Li explicitly ask whether joint RMST fusion improves on inverse-variance combination in their Section 6. Their point-survival analysis does not supply the proposed law-level equality frontier or its full-support endpoint computation.
fill: Characterize scalar information loss using the shared event-law tangent, compute its size through a certified weak boundary problem, and resolve the constructive uniform-inference bottleneck without supplying any nuisance function or imposing a nuisance-rate assumption.
